audit_items.title: Verify Merkle Proof Construction - Correct Generalized Index
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java at lines 324-328. The generalized index for blob_kzg_commitments is computed dynamically from the SSZ schema structure.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The getBlockBodyKzgCommitmentsGeneralizedIndex() method retrieves the index from BeaconBlockBodySchemaElectra using getChildGeneralizedIndex(getFieldIndex(BlockBodyFields.BLOB_KZG_COMMITMENTS)). This approach ensures the index is automatically correct for each fork by deriving it from the SSZ schema rather than using hardcoded values. The verifyDataColumnSidecarInclusionProof() at lines 312-322 correctly uses this index with isValidMerkleBranch.
audit_items.notes: Generalized index is schema-derived, not hardcoded, ensuring correctness across forks.

audit_items.title: Verify Subnet Mapping for Data Column Sidecars
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 148. The subnet computation uses simple modular arithmetic.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The computeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar() method returns columnIndex.mod(specConfigFulu.getDataColumnSidecarSubnetCount()). This is a straightforward, deterministic modular arithmetic operation that correctly maps column indices to subnets according to the specification. The implementation is simple and correct with no edge cases.
audit_items.notes: Simple modular arithmetic implementation matches specification.

audit_items.title: Verify Sidecar Retention Period
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 607. Checks if data column sidecars are required for a given epoch.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The isAvailabilityOfDataColumnSidecarsRequiredAtEpoch() method correctly implements the retention check using currentEpoch.minusMinZero(epoch).isLessThanOrEqualTo(specConfigFulu.getMinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequests()). This uses the specification constant MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS and correctly computes the epoch difference with underflow protection.
audit_items.notes: Correctly uses spec constant for retention period calculation.

audit_items.title: Validate BLS Field Elements - Reject Values >= BLS_MODULUS
audit_items.phase1_summary: The bytes_to_bls_field function is not implemented in Teku Java code. BLS field operations are delegated to native C-KZG or Rust-KZG libraries.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: While KZG.java defines BLS_MODULUS as a constant, the actual validation of field elements happens in the external native library (C-KZG4844 or Rust-KZG). Teku does not implement the low-level BLS field arithmetic or validation. This check falls outside the scope of the Teku codebase audit.
audit_items.notes: Field element validation is handled by external native KZG library.

audit_items.title: Verify compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs Time Budget
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in CKZG4844.java at line 168. The function delegates to native library implementation.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The computeCellsAndKzgProofs() method in CKZG4844.java delegates to CKZG4844JNI.computeCellsAndKzgProofs(). The actual polynomial operations and performance characteristics are implemented in the native C-KZG library. Teku does not implement the polynomial math or control the execution time of this operation.
audit_items.notes: Performance is determined by external native library implementation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trusted Setup Documentation and Integrity
audit_items.phase1_summary: This item concerns the documentation and ceremony process for the KZG trusted setup, not code implementation.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The trusted setup is a one-time ceremony that generates public parameters for the KZG commitment scheme. This is a protocol-level concern about documentation, ceremony procedures, and parameter distribution. It is not a code implementation issue that can be verified in the Teku codebase.
audit_items.notes: Documentation and ceremony concern, not code implementation.

audit_items.title: Batch Verification Detects Tampered Evaluation Data
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in CKZG4844.java at line 182 and MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 266. Cryptographic verification delegated to native library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The verifyCellKzgProofBatch() method in CKZG4844.java delegates to CKZG4844JNI.verifyCellKzgProofBatch(). Teku's verifyDataColumnSidecarKzgProofs() correctly passes commitments, cells with column IDs, and proofs to the native library. The actual cryptographic verification that detects tampering is implemented in the native KZG library, not in Teku Java code.
audit_items.notes: Cryptographic verification implemented in native library.

audit_items.title: Prevent Proof Reuse Across Different Cells/Commitments
audit_items.phase1_summary: Cryptographic binding between proofs and cells is enforced by the native KZG library verification functions.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The cryptographic property that binds a proof to a specific cell and commitment is enforced by the KZG proof verification algorithm implemented in the native library. Teku correctly passes per-cell data (commitment, cell index, cell data, proof) to the verification functions, but the cryptographic guarantee against proof reuse is a property of the native implementation.
audit_items.notes: Cryptographic binding property of native KZG library.

audit_items.title: Detect Mutually Inconsistent Recovery Cells
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in CKZG4844.java at line 205 and MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 492. Recovery and verification delegated to native library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The recoverCellsAndProofs() method in CKZG4844.java delegates to the native library. Teku's reconstructAllDataColumnSidecars() in MiscHelpersFulu.java checks that at least numberOfColumns/2 cells are available before attempting recovery. The native library performs post-recovery verification to ensure consistency. The cryptographic detection of inconsistent cells is handled by the native implementation.
audit_items.notes: Cryptographic recovery verification in native library.

audit_items.title: Selective Subnet Censorship Cannot Reduce Availability Below 50%
audit_items.phase1_summary: This is a network topology and protocol design question about the data availability sampling scheme.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The concern is whether the subnet distribution and custody requirements can prevent availability from falling below the 50% threshold needed for recovery. This is a protocol-level design property, not a specific implementation detail in the Teku codebase. It depends on the overall network topology and subnet assignment strategy defined in the specification.
audit_items.notes: Protocol design question, not implementation-specific.

audit_items.title: Sidecar Request Rate-Limiting Implementation
audit_items.phase1_summary: P2P networking layer uses libp2p with rate limiting. DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator.java validates sidecars before acceptance.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: Teku uses libp2p which provides built-in rate limiting capabilities. The DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator performs structural and cryptographic validation before accepting gossip messages. However, rate limiting for RPC-based sidecar requests (BeaconBlocksByRange, BeaconBlocksByRoot equivalents for sidecars) needs specific verification to ensure it is properly configured and enforced separately from gossip validation.
audit_items.notes: Gossip validation present, but RPC-level rate limiting needs verification.

audit_items.title: Prevent Custody Group Membership Inference
audit_items.phase1_summary: This is a protocol-level privacy concern about side-channel analysis of validator behavior.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The concern is whether an adversary can infer which custody groups a validator belongs to by observing network behavior, request patterns, or timing. This is a protocol design and network-level privacy question, not a specific code implementation issue. Mitigation would involve protocol-level design decisions about request patterns and anonymity.
audit_items.notes: Protocol-level privacy concern, not code implementation.

audit_items.title: Custody Requirements Computed from Finalized State Only
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in CustodyGroupCountManagerImpl.java at line 215 and MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 217. Custody computation uses BeaconState passed by caller.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The computeCustodyColumnIndices() method uses getValidatorsCustodyRequirement() which takes a BeaconState parameter. The actual state used depends on what the caller passes. To ensure custody requirements are based only on finalized state (preventing manipulation via unfinalized state), verification is needed that all callers pass finalized checkpoint state. The implementation itself is correct, but the caller context needs verification.
audit_items.notes: Need to verify callers use finalized state for custody computation.

audit_items.title: Validate blobs_bundle.proofs Length Before Slicing
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in BlobsBundleFulu.java at lines 45-49. Validates proof count matches expected cells per blob.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The BlobsBundleFulu constructor contains checkArgument(proofs.size() == blobs.size() * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) which validates that the number of proofs matches the expected count based on the number of blobs and cells per blob. This validation occurs before any slicing or indexing operations, preventing out-of-bounds access. The implementation is correct and safe.
audit_items.notes: Proof count validation present before slicing operations.

audit_items.title: Correct blob_kzg_commitments Index for Fulu Fork
audit_items.phase1_summary: Same as CHK-0022. Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java at lines 324-328. Generalized index computed from SSZ schema.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The getBlockBodyKzgCommitmentsGeneralizedIndex() method retrieves the index dynamically from the SSZ schema structure using getChildGeneralizedIndex(getFieldIndex(BlockBodyFields.BLOB_KZG_COMMITMENTS)). This ensures the index is automatically correct for the Fulu fork and any future forks by deriving it from the actual schema rather than using hardcoded values. The implementation handles fork-specific schema changes correctly.
audit_items.notes: Schema-derived index ensures correctness across forks.

audit_items.title: Incorrect Inverse FFT Produces Higher-Degree Polynomials
audit_items.phase1_summary: FFT and inverse FFT operations are implemented in the native KZG library, not in Teku Java code.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The Fast Fourier Transform and its inverse are fundamental polynomial operations used in the KZG commitment scheme. These operations are implemented in the native C-KZG or Rust-KZG library. Teku does not implement polynomial arithmetic or FFT operations in Java code. Verification of correct FFT implementation falls outside the scope of the Teku audit.
audit_items.notes: FFT operations implemented in native library.

audit_items.title: Recovery with Minimum Cells Meets Time Bounds
audit_items.phase1_summary: Performance of the recoverCellsAndProofs operation in the native KZG library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The time complexity and performance characteristics of cell recovery using the minimum required number of cells (50% + 1) are determined by the native library implementation. Teku delegates to the native library for recovery operations. Performance testing and optimization of the recovery algorithm are the responsibility of the native library, not the Teku codebase.
audit_items.notes: Native library performance characteristic.

audit_items.title: Division by Zero Prevention in Recovery
audit_items.phase1_summary: Recovery mathematics including division operations are implemented in the native KZG library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The recovery algorithm involves interpolation and evaluation operations that may include division. Protection against division by zero and handling of edge cases in the mathematical operations are implemented in the native C-KZG or Rust-KZG library. Teku does not implement the recovery mathematics in Java code.
audit_items.notes: Recovery math implemented in native library.

audit_items.title: Data Withholding Attack Detectability
audit_items.phase1_summary: This is a protocol design question about the game-theoretic properties of the data availability sampling scheme.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The concern is whether data withholding attacks (where a proposer publishes an invalid block but withholds some data) can be reliably detected by honest validators through the custody and sampling scheme. This is a protocol-level security property that depends on the overall design of the data availability layer, not a specific implementation detail in the Teku codebase.
audit_items.notes: Protocol design security property.

audit_items.title: Low-Balance Validators Assigned Minimum Custody Groups
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java at line 231. Custody group count calculation includes minimum floor.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The getValidatorsCustodyRequirement() method computes custody group count using count.max(specConfigFulu.getValidatorCustodyRequirement()).min(specConfigFulu.getNumberOfCustodyGroups()). The .max(validatorCustodyRequirement) operation ensures that validators are assigned at least the minimum number of custody groups regardless of their effective balance. This correctly implements the specification requirement for minimum custody participation.
audit_items.notes: Minimum custody requirement correctly enforced.

audit_items.title: Bit-Reversal Permutation Applied Consistently
audit_items.phase1_summary: BRP (bit-reversal permutation) is applied during polynomial operations in the native KZG library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The bit-reversal permutation is a mathematical transformation used in FFT-based polynomial operations. This is implemented in the native C-KZG or Rust-KZG library as part of the polynomial arithmetic operations. Teku does not implement polynomial operations or BRP in Java code. Verification of consistent BRP application is the responsibility of the native library.
audit_items.notes: BRP implemented in native library polynomial operations.

audit_items.title: Batch Verification Resource Cost Bounded
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in CKZG4844.java. The verifyCellProofBatch() method does not enforce a maximum batch size limit.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The verifyCellProofBatch() method in CKZG4844.java does not explicitly limit the batch size for verification operations. The batch size depends on the number of cells passed by the caller. While callers like verifyDataColumnSidecarKzgProofsBatch in MiscHelpersFulu are invoked from gossip validation which processes sidecars in bounded groups, there is no explicit hard limit in the KZG interface itself to prevent resource exhaustion from excessively large batches.
audit_items.notes: No explicit batch size limit in KZG verification interface.

audit_items.title: hash_to_bls_field Collision Resistance
audit_items.phase1_summary: The hash_to_bls_field function is implemented in the native KZG library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The hash_to_bls_field function maps arbitrary byte strings to BLS field elements in a collision-resistant manner. This is a cryptographic primitive implemented in the native C-KZG or Rust-KZG library. The collision resistance property depends on the underlying hash function and domain separation used in the native implementation. This is outside the scope of the Teku codebase audit.
audit_items.notes: Cryptographic primitive in native library.

audit_items.title: Pairing Check Rejects Invalid Proofs
audit_items.phase1_summary: Pairing operations for KZG proof verification are implemented in the native KZG library.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The pairing check is the core cryptographic operation that verifies KZG proofs. It uses bilinear pairings on the BLS12-381 elliptic curve. This operation is implemented in the native C-KZG or Rust-KZG library. The correctness of the pairing computation and its ability to reject invalid proofs is a property of the native cryptographic implementation, not the Teku Java code.
audit_items.notes: Pairing operations in native library.

audit_items.title: BLS12-381 Bilinear Diffie-Hellman Assumption Maintained
audit_items.phase1_summary: This concerns the cryptographic hardness assumption underlying the KZG commitment scheme.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The security of KZG commitments relies on the computational hardness of the bilinear Diffie-Hellman problem on the BLS12-381 curve. This is a cryptographic assumption about the mathematical structure of the elliptic curve, not an implementation property. It is a foundational assumption of the protocol specification, not something that can be verified in code.
audit_items.notes: Cryptographic hardness assumption, not implementation.

audit_items.title: Total node balance computation overflow safety
audit_items.phase1_summary: Located in MiscHelpersFulu.java line 221-228, getValidatorsCustodyRequirement() computes totalNodeBalance by summing effective balances using UInt64 arithmetic.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The computation uses stream reduce with UInt64::plus to sum validator effective balances. Maximum possible value is ~1M validators * 32 ETH = ~32*10^15 Gwei, well within UInt64 max (~1.8*10^19). While UInt64 wraps on overflow rather than throwing, overflow is not practically achievable with consensus protocol constraints.
audit_items.notes: Mathematical analysis confirms total balance cannot overflow UInt64 bounds under protocol constraints.

audit_items.title: Fork epoch constants strict ordering
audit_items.phase1_summary: MiscHelpers.java line 76-93 implements computeForkVersion() using if-else cascade checking fork epochs in descending order from Gloas down to Genesis.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: The implementation uses descending epoch checks (Gloas >= Fulu >= Electra >= Deneb >= Capella >= Bellatrix >= Altair >= Genesis). Fork epoch values are loaded from YAML configuration and validated during SpecConfig initialization. The if-else structure ensures correct version selection regardless of constant values.
audit_items.notes: Config validation ensures proper ordering; if-else structure handles any valid configuration correctly.

audit_items.title: Compute fork version returns exactly one version
audit_items.phase1_summary: The computeForkVersion() method in MiscHelpers.java uses mutually exclusive if-else cascade with exhaustive coverage.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: Each epoch comparison is mutually exclusive (>=) and the cascade is exhaustive with a final genesis fallback. Every possible epoch value maps to exactly one fork version. No epoch can satisfy multiple conditions simultaneously.
audit_items.notes: Mutually exclusive conditions with exhaustive fallback guarantee exactly one version per epoch.

audit_items.title: Compute fork version edge-case epoch handling
audit_items.phase1_summary: The method uses UInt64.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo() comparisons which handle boundary values including 0 and UInt64.MAX_VALUE.
audit_items.phase2_assessment: UInt64 comparisons correctly handle epoch=0 (falls through to genesis), UInt64.MAX_VALUE (matches first branch if fork epoch not FAR_FUTURE), and all intermediate values. UInt64 cannot be negative. The genesis fallback ensures all edge cases return a valid version.
audit_items.notes: UInt64 semantics and exhaustive fallback handle all edge cases correctly.

audit_items.phase2_assessment: Teku receives deposit requests via Engine API from the EL client as already-parsed DepositRequest objects. The raw ABI parsing and offset validation happens in the EL client implementation. Teku uses ExecutionRequestsDataCodec.decode() for SSZ deserialization only.

audit_items.title: Deposit requests accumulator concatenates all valid data

audit_items.phase2_assessment: The encode() method uses SSZ serialization (sszSerialize()) which is deterministic and prepends the request type byte. The decode() method validates strict ascending order of request types. SSZ serialization ensures deterministic concatenation of deposit data. The actual accumulation from logs occurs EL-side, but CL encoding/decoding is correct.
audit_items.notes: CL-side SSZ encoding/decoding is deterministic and validates ordering; EL handles log accumulation.
